segments.text: There is a prophecy in Sahih al-Bukhari about money. Not a crash... not poverty. The opposite. A day when a man will carry his charity through the streets... and come home still holding it.
segments._shot: coins spilling across a dark table, slow

segments.text: This is the prophecy... of the unwanted gold.
segments.title: THE UNWANTED GOLD
segments._shot: slow golden dust settling on black

segments.text: To feel the weight of this, remember who first heard it. Madinah was a city of date farmers and shepherds who knew famine years by name. Charity... zakat... is a pillar of Islam, and in that world there was never any difficulty finding a hand open to receive it.
segments._shot: dry palm grove in harsh noon light

segments.text: And into that world the Prophet, peace be upon him, said... the Hour will not be established until your wealth increases so much... that a man will be worried... because no one will accept his zakat. The person he offers it to will answer... I am not in need of it.
segments._shot: overflowing grain pouring past the edges of a bowl

segments.text: In another narration he pressed it further... give in charity now, for a time will come when a man will wander about with his charity, and the answer will be... if you had brought it yesterday, I would have taken it. But today... I am not in need of it.
segments._shot: empty market street at golden hour

segments.text: A prophecy about too much money, spoken to people who had almost none. No politician promises abundance as a warning. He did... because the test of full hands is harder than the test of empty ones.
segments._shot: hands-free image: light flooding an empty room

segments.text: The instruction inside the prophecy is one word... NOW. Give now, while someone still needs it. Generosity has an expiry date... and only Allah knows when.
